findings.title: Test Coverage Gap: SSE Status Endpoint Missing Ownership Verification
findings.description: While the tests cover audit routes and artifact retrieval, there are no tests for the SSE status endpoint (/api/status/{scan_id}) which neighbor findings indicate lacks user ownership verification. Any authenticated user could potentially stream status for any scan_id.
findings.suggested_fix: Add test cases for SSE status endpoint that verify: 1) User can only stream status for their own scans, 2) Accessing another user's scan_id returns 403/404. This would require testing the stream_status endpoint from api/routes/status.py.

findings.title: Test Coverage Gap: Webhook Replay Detection Scaling Not Verified
findings.description: The tests verify webhook replay detection works within a single test instance (using setUp to clear _seen_deliveries), but do not verify that replay detection works across multiple API instances. The neighbor findings indicate _seen_deliveries uses in-memory storage which doesn't scale horizontally.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note or integration test documenting that webhook replay detection currently only works within a single API instance. For production deployments requiring multiple instances, consider using a distributed cache (Redis) for _seen_deliveries.

findings.title: Test Coverage Gap: OAuth State Secret Reuse Not Tested
findings.description: The tests for GitHub OAuth verify the happy path but do not test the fallback behavior where OAuth state secret falls back to JWT secret. Neighbor findings indicate that _state_secret() falls back to supabase_jwt_secret which is a security concern.
findings.suggested_fix: Add test case that mocks settings.github_oauth_state_secret as None/unset and verifies the system either: 1) Uses a separate secure default, or 2) Refuses to operate without explicit configuration (fail closed).

findings.title: Potential Information Disclosure in FORGE Integration Tests
findings.description: The test_forge_bridge.py tests send tier1_findings including severity levels to external FORGE service. While this is test code, it demonstrates that findings with severity 'critical' are sent to an external service. If production code follows this pattern, sensitive finding details could be exposed to external services.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify that production code sanitizes or filters sensitive data before sending to external FORGE service. Consider whether severity levels and finding titles should be sent externally, or if only anonymized/faggregated data should be transmitted.

findings.title: Test environment setup causes side effects at import time
findings.description: Multiple test files set environment variables using os.environ.setdefault() at module import time (lines 11-17 in test_audit_routes.py, similar pattern in other test files). This causes side effects during import that can leak between test modules and affect other tests running in the same Python process. Additionally, the fake orchestrator module creation (lines 25-35) modifies sys.modules during import, which is a global side effect.
findings.suggested_fix: Move environment variable setup to a pytest fixture with autouse=True or to a conftest.py file. Create the fake orchestrator in a test fixture that uses monkeypatch to temporarily modify sys.modules and cleans up afterward. Use pytest-env or similar plugin for environment variable management.

findings.title: Tests directly access production module global state

This creates tight coupling between tests and implementation details - any refactoring of internal state will break tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Instead of accessing internal state, inject a cleanup mechanism into the production code (e.g., a function like reset_replay_detection() or use dependency injection). Alternatively, expose configuration for test isolation through a proper interface.

findings.title: Duplicated FastAPI test app setup across test classes
findings.description: Each test file (test_audit_routes.py, test_fix_routes.py, test_github_oauth_routes.py, test_onboarding_routes.py, test_webhook_routes.py) contains nearly identical FastAPI app setup code in setUpClass: creating app, setting up limiter, adding middleware to inject user_id, including router. findings.suggested_fix: Create a shared test fixture in conftest.py that returns a TestClient with properly configured app. Use pytest fixtures with proper scoping to avoid test pollution. Example: @pytest.fixture(scope="class") def audit_client(): ... that can be parameterized for different routers.

findings.title: Test uses hardcoded mock paths brittle to refactoring
findings.description: Tests use hardcoded module paths for mocking like 'api.routes.audit.db.get_github_access_token', 'api.routes.fix.db.get_action_item', etc. These string-based patches are tightly coupled to the specific import paths in production code. If the production code refactors imports (e.g., moves db to a different module or uses dependency injection), all these mock paths will break.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider using dependency injection in production code to allow injecting mock implementations. Alternatively, create a test db interface that can be patched at a higher level. Use unittest.mock.patch.object when possible instead of string-based paths.

findings.title: Fake orchestrator workaround indicates production dependency issue

findings.suggested_fix: Refactor production code to remove direct import of orchestrator in audit routes - use lazy imports or dependency injection. findings.title: Test directly couples to implementation details like limiter

findings.title: Regex patterns as module-level constants reduce configurability
findings.description: All security patterns (SECRET_PATTERNS, DANGEROUS_PATTERNS, SQL_PATTERNS, etc.) are hardcoded as module-level constants in indexer.py. While this provides deterministic scanning, it makes the scanner less adaptable to different security policies without code changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider making patterns configurable via settings or a configuration file. This would allow different security policies per deployment without code changes.

findings.title: Cross-segment coupling: tier1 depends on models from seg-models-1
findings.description: The orchestrator imports directly from models.findings (AuditReport, Finding, Category, Severity, FindingSource) and models.scan (PrimerResult). This creates bidirectional dependency risk with seg-models-1. If models change, tier1 breaks.

locations.snippet:
from models.findings import AuditReport, Category, Finding, FindingSource, Severity
from models.scan import PrimerResult

findings.suggested_fix: Use dependency injection for model imports. Define interfaces/abstractions that tier1 owns, and let seg-models-1 implement adapters. Alternatively, move the conversion logic to a separate module that both segments depend on.

findings.title: Cross-segment coupling: tier1 depends on services from seg-services-4
findings.description: The tier1 segment directly imports from services.github (get_head_sha, get_repo_info, parse_repo_url). This creates dependency on seg-services-4. The orchestrator uses these services to gather repository metadata before invoking tier1 operations.

locations.snippet: from services.github import get_head_sha, get_repo_info, parse_repo_url

findings.suggested_fix: Define a RepositoryService interface in tier1 contracts. Inject the concrete GitHub service implementation. This enables testing with mock services and reduces coupling.

findings.title: Silent fallback in reporter reduces observability
findings.description: In reporter.py, when the LLM assistant context generation fails, the code catches the exception and continues with fallback_used=True but only logs at exception level. This silent failure may mask significant issues and makes it hard to distinguish between minor and major failures in production monitoring.
findings.suggested_fix: Add metrics/observability for fallback events. Consider distinguishing between transient failures (retry) vs permanent failures (use fallback). Add an alert threshold for fallback rate.
